title: Security & Compliance Controlbook: RBAC, Audit, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary
-------
This controlbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational security and compliance policies for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It provides prescriptive standards, owner assignments, SLOs/thresholds, and pragmatic runbook steps for teams to achieve and demonstrate compliance for customer and regulatory needs.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood-hosted and customer-dedicated/private control plane components, internal tooling, and development workflows. Not intended for vendor-specific legal contracts (see finance-and-legal).

Principles
----------
- Least privilege by default; role-based access with scoped approvals.
- Immutable audit trail for all security-relevant events with tamper-evident retention.
- Region-aware data handling with explicit residency controls.
- Security gates embedded in SDLC (automated tests + human review).
- Clear ownership and measurable evidence for compliance requests.

Owners and SLAs
---------------
- Global security owner: Maya Thompson (security) \u2014 policy authoring and escalation.
- RBAC & Auth owner: Priya Desai (identity team).
- Audit Logging owner: Ethan Rivera (platform SRE).
- Data Residency & Retention owner: Compliance team (work with product/legal).
- Incident Response owner: Security Incident Response (SIR) rotation.
- Evidence workflows owner: GRC team.

SLOs / Thresholds
-----------------
- Audit log availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Audit ingestion latency: 95th percentile < 30s for control-plane events.
- Retention compliance SLA: evidence delivered for audits within 10 business days.
- RBAC policy drift: automated review runs weekly; exceptions > 7 days require approver.

1) RBAC & Authentication
-------------------------
Overview:
- Use centralized identity (OIDC + SAML) with SCIM provisioning for employee and service identities.
- Roles: Admin, Platform-Operator, DBA, Developer, Read-Only, Customer-Admin (for Dedicated/Private).
- Support for short-lived credentials (OIDC tokens), MFA enforced for interactive logins, and hardware-backed keys for high privilege.

Role matrix (high level):
- Admin: full control, requires 2-person approval for elevation.
- Platform-Operator: deploy/run infra components (no billing).
- Developer: code commit, feature toggles in non-prod.
- Read-Only: dashboards, logs only.

Policy & Processes:
- Access request flow: request -> manager approval -> security review (for high privilege) -> provisioning via SCIM.
- Quarterly access review owned by team leads; automated reports generated monthly.
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS or short-lived signed JWTs; secrets stored in KMS/HSM and rotated every 90 days by default.

Example: SCIM provisioning snippet (consolidated):
- Ensure group mapping: scim_groups -> platform-operator.
- Automate deprovisioning: on SSO deactivation, remove all API keys and sessions within 1 hour.

2) Audit Logging
----------------
What we log:
- Auth events: logins, MFA events, token issuance and revocation.
- Authorization decisions: allow/deny per resource/request.
- Administrative actions: role changes, policy edits, key creations/rotations.
- Data access: read/write operations on customer data, export/download events.
- System changes: deploys, schema migrations, infra changes.

Log format & transport:
- Structured JSON with standard fields: timestamp, service, host, principal_id, request_id, action, resource, result, context.
- Transport via secure syslog/HTTPS to centralized logging cluster with immutability (WORM) support for retention windows.

Retention & protection:
- Default control-plane logs: 1 year hot, 3 years cold.
- Customer-sensitive logs: configurable per-customer (regional retention) \u2014 minimum 90 days unless contract specifies more.
- Tamper detection: periodic checksums and signed manifests; alerts on integrity failures.

Audit access and monitoring:
- Read access to audit logs is RBAC controlled; only Security and SRE on-call have elevated read/search privileges.
- Alerting: failed auth spikes, anomalous admin changes, export of large volume of customer data trigger high-severity pager.

Example audit JSON (single line):
{"timestamp":"2026-12-01T15:22:34Z","service":"control-plane-auth","principal_id":"u_12345","action":"token.revoke","resource":"api-key:svc-67","result":"success","request_id":"req_abc123"}

3) Data Residency & Retention
-----------------------------
Policy:
- Customer data stored and processed within customer-specified regions. Default: multi-region US and EU for hosted accounts.
- Data classification: PII, non-PII, aggregate telemetry. Handling rules differ by class.

Residency controls:
- Deployment-time region pinning for Dedicated & Private.
- Data-at-rest encryption with region-specific KMS keys.
- Cross-region replication requires customer opt-in and is logged as export.

Retention matrix (summary):
- Control-plane operational telemetry: 90 days (hot), 2 years (cold).
- Audit logs: 1 year (hot), 3 years (cold) or as contractually required.
- Customer generated content: per-customer contract (default 30 days unless retention product purchased).

Data deletion & eDiscovery:
- Deletion requests: standard request flow -> verification -> purge from primary and dependent caches within 30 days; residual backups retained per retention policy and documented.
- eDiscovery: legal & compliance coordinate with engineering for hold; exports are audited.

4) Secure SDLC
--------------
Gates and tooling:
- CI pipeline enforces: unit tests, SCA (software composition analysis), SAST, secrets scanning, dependency pinning, and license checks.
- Pre-merge checks required for prod-impacting changes.
- Production deploys require canary + automated rollback on error budget breach.

Developer responsibilities:
- Use feature flags for rollout; follow runbook for feature disable.
- Author a short security impact note on PRs touching auth/data planes.

Release checklist (must pass):
1. SAST score: no critical findings.
2. Dependencies: no critical CVEs unmitigated.
3. Secrets: no plaintext secrets in repo.
4. Rollback plan documented.

5) Incident Response (Security)
-------------------------------
Overview:
- SIR rotation runs 24/7 paging for high-severity incidents. Incident severity definitions map to customer impact and data exposure.

Detection & Triage:
- Alerts from IDS, anomaly detectors, audit log heuristics, or external reports get ingested into our incident system.
- Triage checklist: confirm, scope, contain, notify.

Containment & Forensics:
- Short-lived containment: revoke credentials, isolate hosts, freeze deployments.
- Preserve evidence: snapshot disks, export signed audit logs, collect process memory where lawful.
- Chain-of-custody log required for all artifacts used in forensic analysis.

Communication:
- Internal: incident bridge, Slack #incident-{id}, status updates cadence (T+15m, T+60m, T+4h).
- External: customer-notification templates and regulator-specific templates. Legal and CRO engaged for data-exfiltration incidents.

Post-incident:
- Postmortem published within 7 business days for Sev2/1 with action owners and timelines.
- Root cause, mitigations, detection tuning, and verification plan included.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
--------------------------------
Goals:
- Provide automated, reproducible evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO, customer ATOs).

Artifact inventory (examples):
- RBAC reports: current role bindings, recent access reviews.
- Audit logs export: signed time-range manifests.
- Change history: Terraform state and deploy CI run IDs.
- SDLC artifacts: PRs, CI pass logs, SAST reports.

Workflow:
1. Evidence request intake -> GRC ticket created.
2. Automated collection scripts run (where available) to fetch signed artifacts.
3. Manual verification by owner (SRE/security/product).
4. Delivery to auditor/customer, tracking via ticket.

Turnaround and automation:
- Target: automated evidence pulls for standard items within 48 hours.
- Non-automated evidence: 10 business days.

7) Risk & Exceptions
---------------------
Risk acceptance process:
- Teams submit Risk Exception Form (template in confluence).
- Required fields: business justification, compensating controls, duration, mitigation plan, approver.
- Exceptions > 90 days require quarterly renewal and executive-level signoff.

Compensating controls examples:
- Temporary elevated access -> require session recording + MFA + time-limited keys.
- Delayed patching -> increased monitoring and host isolation.

Approval authorities:
- Day-to-day: Security Manager.
- High risk or long duration: Head of Security + Legal + CTO.

Appendices & References
----------------------
- CLI snippets for log export and evidence collection.
- Links to RBAC group naming conventions, SCIM mappings, and SSO provider runbooks.
- Template: Risk Exception Form and Incident Notification templates.

Example: one-line export command for audit logs (platform tooling):
- ./redwoodctl logs export --service control-plane-auth --from 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-11-30T23:59:59Z --sign --out audit-nov-2026.jsonl

Maintenance & Review
--------------------
- Policy review cadence: annually or after a major incident.
- Quarterly tabletop exercises for incident response with product and SRE teams.

Questions / Clarifications
-------------------------
Contact: Maya Thompson (security) \u2014 security@redwood.com. For RBAC provisioning questions contact: Priya Desai (identity).

This controlbook is intended as a living document; proposed edits should follow the Confluence edit workflow and include reviewer assignment to SRE and Security.
